goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that on line 125, the code changes from `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`. Using async callbacks with forEach means the promises returned by the async function are not awaited - forEach ignores return values. This means: 1) The function will complete before the calendar deletions finish, 2) Any errors thrown inside the async callback (including from the await getCalendar or calendar?.deleteEvent) will become unhandled promise rejections that bypass the surrounding try/catch block. This is a real bug introduced by the diff.
